IMPORTANT PUBLIC HEALTH AND SAFETY MESSAGE REGARDING
PARTICIPATION AT CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS
AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 VIRUS, AND RESULTING ORDERS AND DIRECTION FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND THE ORANGE COUNTY HEALTH CARE AGENCY, AS WELL AS THE CITY OF IRVINE EMERGENCY DECLARATION, THE PUBLIC WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO PHYSICALLY ATTEND THE IRVINE CITY COUNCIL MEETING TO WHICH THIS AGENDA APPLIES.
THE MEETING IS BROADCAST LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO "ATTN: CITY COUNCIL," ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE,CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. E-COMMENTS SUBMITTED AT LEAST TWO HOURS PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENTS OF THE MEETING WILL BE DISTRIBUTED TO CITY COUNCILMEMBERS AT THE MEETING. YOU MAY ALSO PROVIDE LIVE COMMENTS VIA "ZOOM." FOR MORE INFORMATION, VISIT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV AND SELECT "CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS."
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. FOR QUESTIONS OR ASSISTANCE, PLEASE CONTACT THE CITY CLERK'S OFFICE AT 949-724-6205, OR VIA EMAIL AT CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF WRITTEN COMMENTS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING.

LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.

Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  April 27, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:12 p.m. on April
27, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran*
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
  *Via teleconference

Mayor Khan announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications
Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, members of the public had the ability to provide live comments on agenda
items using Zoom. Mayor Khan also assured the community that the City of Irvine was
adhering to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City
Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

In addition, Carl Petersen, City Clerk, provided instructions on how to submit live
comments via Zoom; and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended for all
agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on
all agenda items, and would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the
City’s website.
 City Council Minutes  April 27, 2021

  Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
  not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Mayor Kim led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Councilmember Kuo provided the invocation.

  1.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  1.1  Proclaim May - October 2021 as the Orange County Fire Authority's
  "Drowning Prevention Awareness"

  Mayor Khan introduced Shane Sherwood, Division Chief from the
  Orange County Fire Authority, and presented a proclamation
  recognizing May through October 2021 as Orange County Fire
  Authority’s “Drowning Prevention Awareness.”

  Division Chief Sherwood presented a brief public service announcement
  related to drowning safety and prevention, and expressed his
  appreciation for the proclamation.

  Councilmember Agran expressed his appreciation to Division Chief
  Sherwood, noting that the California State Assembly had recently
  proclaimed the third week of May as “Roxie’s Wish: Drowning
  Prevention Week for Children” in support of drowning prevention; and
  suggested working collaboratively with the Orange County Fire Authority
  to review the City’s policies to further prevent childhood drowning in the
  City.

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  2.1  Neighborhood Watch Update

  Bill Bingham, Police Lieutenant, provided a brief update on the
  Neighborhood Watch Program and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: expressing appreciation to Public
  Safety staff on neighborhood watch efforts; and inquired about how the
  community could create their own neighborhood watch committees.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  April 27, 2021

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  Marianna Marysheva, Interim City Manager, turned to Mike Hamel, Police Chief/Director
  of Public Safety, who noted that staff had recently received inquiries regarding the City’s
  leash laws, and that City staff would be working with the community to address residents’
  concerns.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Kuo requested a brief summary about a recent incident at the shopping
  center on Main and Harvard, to which Police Chief Hamel noted that the incident had
  been captured on video, and that a press release would be issued seeking the public’s
  assistance in identifying the suspects.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  The community is invited to attend a Housing Element Community Workshop on
  Thursday at 5:30 p.m.to learn more about the City’s efforts and to provide input on
  housing in Irvine. Irvine, along with all California cities and counties, is required to
  adequately plan for and meet the housing needs of everyone in the community. In
  the Housing Element Update, the City must identify enough potentially developable
  land suitable for residential use to meet the Regional Housing Needs Assessment
  (RHNA) allocation required by the State. The City’s portion of Southern California
  Association of Governments (SCAG) RHNA for the 2021-2029 Housing Element
  is 23,610 units. A flier with information on the Housing Element Update is available
  in eight languages, and anyone needing language assistance for the community
  meeting can contact Melissa Chao at mchao@cityofirvine.org by April 30 to
  schedule an individualized meeting. To register for the meeting, subscribe for
  updates, or for more information on the Housing Element Update, available in
  multiple languages, visit cityofirvine.org/housingelementupdate.

  •  The City has been recognized for the innovative ways of using geographic
  information system to serve the public and improve internal processes. In a survey
  of 91 public sector GIS programs, the City ranked second in North America. It is
  the first time a U.S. government organization has earned a spot among the top
  three in the survey’s history. To determine the rankings, PSD, the publisher of
  Public Sector Digest, conducted a survey of GIS programs using the Geospatial
  Maturity Index. The index is a standardized annual assessment of maturity and
  capacity with insight into three primary categories of competency: Readiness,
  Implementation, and Impact. The City’s GIS team continually strives for
  excellence, ensuring every City department has an easy way to analyze its data,
  and plays a critical role during emergencies, such as the Silverado Fire. The GIS
  team provided real-time evacuation maps the community relied on during last
  year’s wildfire.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  April 27, 2021

  •  The community is invited to support the City’s adopted 2/11 Marine Battalion by
  donating new baby gifts for expecting Marine families. Donations needed include
  new diapers, wipes, car seats, strollers, and car seat/stroller combos. Donations
  can be sent directly to the Irvine 2/11 Marine Adoption Committee through
  AmazonSmile, or by mail. Local pick-up can also be arranged by emailing
  contact@irvine211marines.org. Additionally, monetary donations are being accepted
  online and via check through May 14. For more information, visit
  cityofirvine.org/211.

  •  Residents and businesses can participate in the National Mayor’s Challenge for
  Water Conservation to conserve water and other resources through April 30 at
  mywaterpledge.com. Members of the community are invited to visit the website
  and commit to conserving water resources. For more information, visit
  cityofirvine.org.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  Interim City Manager Marianna Marysheva noted that Item No. 3.5 (Beverage Sales and
  Sponsorship Agreement with Bottling Group, LLC for Exclusive Citywide Beverage
  Supplier and Sponsor Rights) would be removed from the agenda similarly to its removal
  from the Orange County Great Park Board meeting agenda earlier in the day, and that
  the item would return to the City Council at its May 25, 2021 meeting.

  and unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 3.1 through

  3.9  APPROVAL OF PROJECT REPORT AND ENVIRONMENTAL
  DOCUMENT FOR THE JEFFREY ROAD AT IRVINE CENTER DRIVE
  INTERSECTION IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

  This item was removed for separate discussion at the request of
  Councilmember Agran who requested a brief presentation on the
  proposed project. Councilmember Kuo noted a conflict of interest related
  to real property and left the dais at 4:50 p.m.

  Jaimee Bourgeois, Deputy Director of Transportation, and Melissa
  Dugan, Supervising Transportation Analyst, presented the staff report
  and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: questioning the associated timelines
  for commencement and completion of the project; inquired about
  potential impacts to Woodbridge residents; questioned costs associated
  with the project; inquired about whether additional pedestrian and/or
  bicycle lanes would be added; questioned the differences between a
  pre-right and a standard right turn; inquired about whether the nearby
